steps.action:
The sky appears blue because of a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering, in which sunlight interacts with gas molecules in Earth's atmosphere and shorter wavelengths of light are scattered much more efficiently than longer ones. Since blue light has a shorter wavelength than red or yellow light, it is scattered in all directions across the sky, making the entire sky appear blue to an observer on the ground. At sunrise and sunset, sunlight travels through a thicker layer of atmosphere, scattering away most of the blue light and leaving the longer red and orange wavelengths to dominate.
